value.lineage: femtolisp (2008-, Jeff Bezanson): a compact Lisp with a bytecode compiler, mark-and-sweep GC, tail calls and a numeric tower; the language that bootstraps parts of Julia's front end

value.built_to: evaluate a Lisp by compiling s-expressions to a compact bytecode and running them on a stack VM with garbage collection -- small and fast enough to embed and to bootstrap a larger language
value.pressure: the interpretation overhead of naive tree-walking; the memory pressure of a numeric tower; correctness of tail calls and GC
value.success_means: Lisp programs compile and run correctly and quickly; its own test suite passes

cut.note: a small Lisp whose compiler is written in the Lisp itself and whose runtime is a C bytecode interpreter: the compiler (compiler.lsp) emits bytecode into a code object with a constant table; the interpreter (apply_cl) runs a stack machine with explicit frames (environment, previous frame, argument count, captured flag) and computed-goto dispatch when available; a boot image (flisp.boot) holds the compiled compiler so the system starts without interpreting source; a mark-and-sweep collector with a handle stack protects C-held references

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: apply_cl (934-1000): func from the stack, ip from fn_bcode, stack growth check from the code's declared depth, the frame push (fn_env, curr_frame, nargs, ip slot, captured), OP(OP_ARGC) and the 59 opcode cases; USE_COMPUTED_GOTO
organs.mechanism: calling a closure pushes its environment, the caller's frame pointer, the argument count and a flag saying whether the frame's variables have been captured by an inner closure (in which case they live in a heap vector, not the stack); the code object declares its maximum stack depth so the check happens once per call; opcodes are dispatched by a jump table of label addresses when the compiler supports it; tail calls reuse the frame (the record's 'tail calls')
organs.input: a closure and arguments on the stack
assumptions: a stack machine with a per-function depth declaration is simple and fast enough; capturing decides at compile time which frames must be heap-allocated
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a Lisp small enough to embed (it bootstraps Julia's parser) with proper tail calls
organs.human_prior: the classic bytecode Lisp/Scheme VM; computed-goto dispatch from the gcc idiom
organs.source_boundary: apply_cl; MEDIUM because the opcode bodies were not read

organs.human_name: compiler.lsp: bcode:code / ctable / nconst / cdepth (52-57), emit (65), compile-sym, compile-if, compile-begin, compile-while, compile-for (245-320); flisp.boot; mkboot0.lsp / mkboot1.lsp; bootstrap.sh
organs.mechanism: the compiler walks source forms with an environment of lexical variables, emitting opcodes and constant-table indices into a growing code vector while tracking the maximum stack depth; special forms each have a compile function; the result is a closure over a code object; because the compiler is itself Lisp, the build compiles it once into flisp.boot (a serialised heap image) that the C runtime loads at start, and rebuilding the image from source is a two-stage bootstrap
assumptions: writing the compiler in the language keeps the C core small; a boot image avoids interpreting the compiler at every start
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the C core is under 3,000 lines with the compiler outside it
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a change to the VM's opcodes requires regenerating the boot image with the old image (the bootstrap chicken-and-egg the two mkboot files handle)
organs.human_prior: the metacircular compiler with a boot image (every self-hosting Lisp since MacLisp)
organs.source_boundary: compiler.lsp and the boot files; CANDIDATE because bodies were not read

rejected_cuts.candidate: gc (mark-and-sweep with a handle stack: 335-410, 525-620), the reader, printer, equal/hash, cvalues (a C-type and foreign-value layer), builtins, operators, iostream, the numeric tower, the examples and the ASCII Mona Lisa
rejected_cuts.note: cvalues (typed C values as first-class Lisp objects) is the part Julia inherited and deserves its own DEEP item

rejected_cuts.evidence: the VM, the compiler and the collector are separable; the atlas's lisp-1-5-ibm7090-1962 cut holds the ancestor's interpreter

pressures.source_evidence: flisp.c apply_cl; compiler.lsp; the boot files
pressures.condition: an organism implements a Lisp for use inside a larger program; the score is core size (lines of C), startup time, and correct tail-call behaviour on deep recursion; the compiler must be part of the system
pressures.resource_or_constraint: a few thousand lines of C; one boot image
pressures.failure_condition: a core too large to embed, a startup that interprets the compiler from source, or stack growth on tail recursion
pressures.world_punishes: a tree-walking interpreter with the compiler in C; no boot image
pressures.world_rewards: a bytecode VM with frame reuse and a self-hosted compiler shipped as an image
pressures.observable_consequence: lines of C in the core, startup time with and without the boot image, and stack depth on a million-iteration tail loop
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: linking an existing large Lisp (which the size score punishes)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given a precompiled image must start in milliseconds; the same system bootstrapped from source must take seconds; a VM without tail-call frame reuse must overflow on the loop: the world must show all three

ancestry_edges.to: Scheme (Sussman & Steele 1975) in design; the atlas's lisp-1-5-ibm7090-1962 is the family's origin
ancestry_edges.note: from the README and the record
